answer: Beacon-bound admission tickets: each identity commits a nonce, then solves a challenge from a later verifiable random beacon that assigns a sparrow-sized shard. Only a valid beacon-bound proof counts as an admission signal, and the unpredictable beacon blocks precomputation. An attacker can let identities wander across attempts, but each identity pays two CPU-seconds and one beacon round, with failed commitments discarded. This makes sybil cost linear per identity.
